measurement_scope: One mixed Linux RuntimeGraphExecutor graph with bounded timer, native, registry-worker, in-process, scheduled-service, and loopback-listener counts; process-local RSS/thread sample only.

fixture.service_handler: accept one record; scheduled pure encode to declared typed event

scope_limits.active_window: duration, exact event-counter deltas, and per-timer progress are measured with synchronized instrumentation; this is not a cross-revision throughput comparison
scope_limits.backpressure: this probe uses capacity-one lossless timer fan-in, but does not assert that it saturated; graph_program_services has a separate observed full-queue cancellation regression
scope_limits.native_processes: finite command launch count is recorded; child RSS/CPU and peak concurrent process-tree size are not measured
scope_limits.program_services: service fixture is pure program-module encoding; no child command or worker is launched by service handlers
scope_limits.registry_workers: ordinary applet workers are retained by the registry pool and are expected to reap when the final registry/executor reference is dropped
scope_limits.remote: loopback fixture only; remote server resources are not measured
scope_limits.rss_and_threads: Rust probe process only; sampled RSS may miss short peaks
scope_limits.system: does not certify machine-wide resource ceilings, disk, power, WAN, desktop, or platform fault behavior
scope_limits.thread_admission: graph actor tasks are capped at the requested actor count; remote event readers are separately capped at eight; the probe adds one resource monitor, one loopback server, and one watchdog, while runtime command I/O helpers have no separate probe-wide thread cap

workers.ownership: registry-shared ordinary applet pool; graph cancellation joins actor tasks, final registry/executor drop reaps retained workers

registry_worker_reap.ownership: registry-shared ordinary applet pool; graph cancellation joins actor tasks, final registry/executor drop reaps retained workers
